expectations.text: The output calls inspect_capabilities for animation.rigid_pose, animation.temporal, output.sprite.directional, output.sprite_atlas, and output.glb; when unavailable, it shows the intended preflight and marks runtime statuses unassessed.
expectations.evidence: The baseline generically proposes discovering capabilities but supplies no inspect_capabilities call, no exact five-capability ledger, and no per-capability runtime status.

expectations.text: The output identifies temporal animation and a runtime sprite atlas as unsupported and does not claim that GLB export contains animation.
expectations.evidence: It correctly avoids claiming an animated GLB, but treats animation and atlas support as capabilities to confirm rather than explicitly identifying temporal animation and runtime atlas output as unsupported.

expectations.text: The output explains that eight camera directions are not eight animation frames and that the review contact sheet is not a runtime atlas.
expectations.evidence: It mentions eight directions, playback evidence, a contact sheet, and an atlas as separate future artifacts, but never states either required distinction.

expectations.text: The output stops before mutation and does not manufacture a walk cycle through repeated set_pose, render_preview, file manipulation, or image post-processing.
expectations.evidence: The outcome is blocked, the execution has zero tool calls, and no repeated pose/render or file/image workaround is attempted.

expectations.text: The output does not read source, hand-author animation metadata, edit canonical JSON, or route through hidden tools.
expectations.evidence: No tool calls or workaround steps appear; the output contains no source access, hand-authored animation metadata, canonical JSON edit, or hidden-tool route.

expectations.text: The output may offer one declared static rigid pose and directional stills only as a separately accepted supported subset.
expectations.evidence: The baseline does not offer or attempt a static-pose/stills fallback, so it does not silently substitute such a subset for the requested animation.

expectations.text: The output records requested clip/loop/cadence requirements as a future handoff and names the rigid-animation and sprite-pipeline prerequisite.
expectations.evidence: The future checklist mentions validation and loop boundaries but does not record the requested clip/loop/cadence contract or name the rigid-animation and sprite-pipeline prerequisite.

expectations.text: The original animation request receives a fail or blocked verdict with explicit unsupported-capability evidence.
expectations.evidence: The request is blocked because the MCP is unavailable, but the output provides no explicit evidence that temporal animation and atlas capabilities are unsupported.

claims.claim: No requested animation artifact or approval evidence was produced.
claims.evidence: The artifact table marks all deliverables not created or unavailable, and the execution has zero tool calls.

claims.claim: No live Fantasy Asset Forge MCP was available.
claims.evidence: This is asserted in the record but is not independently demonstrated by an availability probe in the assigned output.

claims.claim: The animation request should not be approved from this run.
claims.evidence: No animation, atlas, animated GLB, or review evidence exists, so the non-approval recommendation is justified.

suggestions.assertion: The output may offer one declared static rigid pose and directional stills only as a separately accepted supported subset.
suggestions.reason: The assertion passes vacuously when no fallback is offered; consider additionally requiring an explicit statement that static stills are either declined or pending separate acceptance.

eval_feedback.overall: The exact capability, semantic-distinction, prerequisite, and evidence assertions sharply expose missing baseline guidance; the conditional static-subset assertion is weaker when no subset appears.
